notes: Midflight as on main at 6b3caea (the Graph Hacks build plus the scale benchmark), run on October 17, 2026 with the `sonnet` alias of that day. The fixes in the scale-1 to scale-3 branches are not in this run.

Run against a Midflight on the same machine (experiment/local_midflight.py): everything in memory, one person signed in who leads the project and owns every task, the HireBot Pro plan as plan v1 and the lead's change as plan v2. The AI reviewer was scripted, as in B3 and B4, so this run says nothing about the reviewer.

A first attempt (B5) is not counted: three of five agents called Midflight's read-only my_projects tool first, the driver didn't allow it, and they stopped to ask for permission. Bookings never claimed, so the case's conflict never came up. The driver now allows my_projects (commit 4945744).

Phase 1: all claims reviewed; Midflight recorded six assumptions as agreed between tasks (for example app.catalog.get_agent and list_agents, the pricing signature with rush). Nothing reached the lead.

Phase 2: the lead approved plan v2 in Midflight; nothing was pasted to any agent. One escalation, E-21, the real disagreement (a 20% fee against a full refund), sent to the lead with both sides. The lead resolved it once with the fixed decision, then messages 11 and 12 went to T3 and T4.

C13 failed at merge: the report returned HTTP 500 once a booking existed, because reports read bookings' records as dicts while bookings stored model objects. Both sides had stated assumptions about that store; the shape (object or dict) was never pinned down. One fix round.
13 of 14 at merge, 14 of 14 after one fix round. Cost $7.44 and 283 turns, about three times B3: the current model takes many more turns (46 and 48 for pricing and bookings in phase 1).
